title: Kernel ABI + Scheduler Contracts for Mixed-bit Quant Paths
body:
Summary:
This is a working draft that defines a minimal kernel ABI and scheduler contract to support mixed-bit execution paths (INT8/FP8/GPTQ/AWQ/4-bit variants) while preserving safe KV cache semantics and graceful fallback behavior. It focuses on what kernels must declare, which invariants the scheduler relies on, and how the KV cache should be addressed when the execution precision changes mid-session.

Context / motivation:
We keep adding low-bit kernels (GPTQ/AWQ/4-bit) that have different memory layout and numeric behavior. So far each kernel ships with ad-hoc glue and scheduler hints. That approach increases complexity and leads to subtle bugs: KV cache incompatibilities, tokenization differences at the float/quant boundary, and surprising latency regressions when fallback happens. We need a compact, operationally-lean ABI: small capability flags plus a clear set of scheduler responsibilities.

Goals for this document (non-exhaustive):
- Define a small, versioned kernel capability descriptor that kernels expose at load time.
- Specify scheduler guarantees/assumptions when selecting kernels for requests.
- Define KV cache invalidation/compatibility rules for precision transitions.
- Enumerate per-kernel constraints (alignment, workspace size, supported sequence lengths, fused-op compatibility).
- Provide a set of telemetry counters and error-class mappings for graceful rollout and debugging.

Non-goals:
- Final micro-kernel ISA or CUDA kernel code.
- Quantization algorithm details (those live in applied-ml docs).

Kernel capability descriptor (minimal fields):
Each kernel when registered with the runtime must return a capability descriptor (small JSON/YAML blob) with the following keys (flat key:value pairs):
- abi_version: string (e.g., "1") — increments on ABI changes.
- kernel_id: string (unique within image, e.g., "gptq_fused_attn_v2").
- precision: string (one of: "fp32", "fp16", "int8", "fp8_e4m3", "awq4", "gptq4", "int4").
- numeric_profile: string ("deterministic" | "stochastic") — indicates whether the kernel uses deterministic rounding/sgd or non-deterministic techniques (affects debugging and replay).
- kv_cache_compatibility: string ("bitwise" | "semantic" | "none") — see below.
- max_seq_len: integer (max supported sequence length without segmentation).
- min_prefix_align: integer (bytes) — alignment constraint for prefix buffer (important for int4 layouts).
- workspace_bytes: integer — worst-case per-stream scratch needed.
- supports_prefill: boolean (kernel supports a prefill+decode split).
- fused_ops: list of strings (e.g., ["rms_norm", "rotary", "kv_prefetch"]).
- preferred_batching: string ("low_latency" | "high_throughput" | "balanced").
- flags: list of strings (free-form: e.g., ["quant-finebias", "kv-raw-layout"]).

Notes on kv_cache_compatibility semantics:
- bitwise: kernel uses same serialized KV layout and quantization mapping as the hosted fp16 reference; previously cached binary blobs can be used without mutation when switching to this kernel. This is the strongest guarantee and enables instant switchovers.
- semantic: kernel uses equivalent mathematical representation but may differ in bitpacking or biasing; the runtime must perform a fast re-encode pass when switching. Re-encode must be non-blocking (incremental) or done during warmup tokens.
- none: cached KV blobs are incompatible; switching requires cache invalidation and re-prefill.

Scheduler contract (what scheduler must guarantee):
- Kernel selection must be based on request-level policy (latency budget, cost target, region, model pin) and the kernel capability descriptor.
- If kernel.kv_cache_compatibility == "none" and session has prefix tokens cached, scheduler must either:
  - Pin that session to compatible kernels for the session's lifetime, or
  - Trigger a cache re-prefill combined with routing the request to a different replica before accepting user-visible traffic.
- When switching from precision A -> B where kv_cache_compatibility == "semantic", scheduler must ensure an asynchronous re-encode is scheduled before the next decode step consumes the cache. Re-encode must preserve request ordering (no out-of-order token visibility).
- Scheduler must expose a signal that informs request routing about predicted added latency when choosing a kernel that requires re-encode. This feeds the admission controller for latency SLO enforcement.
- The scheduler will treat kernels with preferred_batching == "high_throughput" as candidates for batched lanes and the others as low-latency single-shot lanes. Kernels can be in multiple lanes if they advertise support.

KV cache rules and layout stability:
- The runtime will maintain an internal canonical in-memory KV layout (untagged). Kernels register an adapter for (serialize_deserialize) when kv_cache_compatibility != "bitwise". The adapter must be idempotent and annotatable with the kernel_id used to produce it.
- On a semantic transition, the runtime will:
  1) mark the session as "re-encode in progress" (client-visible request still returns streamed tokens only after encode hits first token; see fallback policy).
  2) schedule a background pass to convert cached per-layer kv buffers using the adapter. This must be interruptible and checkpointed.
  3) if background fails or exceeds configured window, either failover to a pinned compatible replica or fall back to decode-only path with reduced throughput.
- For "none" transitions the runtime will prefer pinned-serving or allocate a new replica and do a fresh prefill.

Memory / alignment and packing constraints (common pitfalls):
- 4-bit packings (awq/gptq) often require nibbles packed into 32-bit words with channel or head-first order. Kernels must declare min_prefix_align so the scheduler can plan DMA/UC copies.
- Some FP8 kernels expect 16-byte alignment on attention matrices due to vector load intrinsic. The scheduler must ensure we don't place misaligned buffers into GPU scratch without a copy.
- Workspace_bytes must be treated as a hard reservation for the lane the kernel is bound to. Oversubscription must be prevented at lane allocation time.

Prefill / decode split semantics:
- Kernels that support prefill decode split must explicitly assert supports_prefill=true. The runtime will then allow asynchronous prefill to populate KV cache and mark session as ready for low-latency decode.
- If a prefill completes and the selected decode kernel is incompatible, scheduler must either prevent decode kernel selection or perform re-encode (see above).

Fallback and graceful degradation patterns (operational):
- Canary rollout: new kernel build is deployed to a small percentage of traffic with canary flag. Telemetry counters to watch: reencode_seconds, kv_incompat_errors, fallback_count, mean_latency_by_lane, tail90_latency_by_lane.
- If reencode_seconds > threshold or kv_incompat_errors spike, the autosafe policy will drain canaries and re-route to a stable kernel.
- Runtime must implement a fast-path "soft pin" that keeps a session on the same kernel until explicit rebind is requested; this avoids repeated conversions for multi-turn sessions.

Telemetry & error taxonomy (minimum):
- kernel_load_time_ms (per kernel_id)
- kernel_mem_reservation_failures (count)
- kv_reencode_time_ms (per session)
- kv_reencode_errors{code} (count)
- kernel_fallback_initiated (count)
- kernel_prefill_mismatch (count)
- decode_latency_ms_by_kernel (histogram tags)
- numeric-drift-alerts (when decode outputs diverge beyond threshold vs fp32 baseline for same prompt) — flagged by evaluation harness.

Operational checklists (for kernel rollout owners):
- Unit tests for serialization roundtrip of KV cache adapter (semantic).
- Perf test: prefill + 10k decode tokens without rebind.
- Memory-pressure test: run mixed lane allocation at 120% target traffic to ensure reservation enforcements.
- Integration smoke: switch session from fp16 -> gptq4 and ensure no token duplication / ordering regressions.

Open questions / unresolved tradeoffs:
- Are we comfortable with a 'soft re-encode' window where the first N decode tokens can be performed by a fallback kernel while background re-encode proceeds? This helps reduce user-facing latency, but complicates token attribution and billing.
- Should kv_cache_compatibility include a minor version field so we can evolve packing without bumping global abi_version?
- How best to signal deterministic vs nondeterministic numeric profiles to higher-level evals to avoid false-positive quality alerts?

Action items / next steps:
- Marco: prototype a small adapter shim that converts between reference fp16 KV layout and gptq4 layout (SERV-1424). Target prototype by 2026-02-15.
- Priya: add a scheduler flag that annotates predicted re-encode latency in route decisions (PR #842).
- Jonah: hook basic telemetry counters (kv_reencode_time_ms, kv_reencode_errors) into Console experiments dashboard.
- Evelyn (owner): review canary gating thresholds and add to rollout playbook.

Notes to self / rough TODOs:
- Consider adding a minimal checksum on KV blobs so incompatibility failures are quick to detect.
- We should standardize on a compact schema for fused_ops names to avoid string mismatch.
- Revisit 'workspace_bytes' semantics for multi-GPU shards vs single GPU lane.

Appendix: sample capability descriptor (line-delimited for kernel authors):
abi_version: 1
kernel_id: awq4_fused_attn_v1
precision: awq4
numeric_profile: deterministic
kv_cache_compatibility: semantic
max_seq_len: 4096
min_prefix_align: 64
workspace_bytes: 268435456
supports_prefill: true
fused_ops: [rms_norm, rotary, kv_prefetch]
preferred_batching: high_throughput
flags: [quant-finebias, requires-prefill-check]

If you disagree with any of the above, leave a comment inline or ping in #eng-serving-runtime. This is intentionally terse — want concrete code-friendly answers rather than long philosophical debates.

References / related: see linked artifacts above and the applied-ml repo notes on gptq packing (internal link in linear ticket SERV-1293).

End of draft.
